title: gree: mint a 1-of-1 NFT with Metaplex metadata in one instruction
summary: One click mints an NFT: the program mints one token, then calls Metaplex to attach its name, symbol and image link and to lock the supply.
what: gree mints a non-fungible token with one instruction. The program creates a new mint with 0 decimals, mints exactly 1 token to your wallet, then makes two cross-program calls (CPIs) into Metaplex Token Metadata: one creates the **metadata** account (name `GLC-20240317`, symbol `GRLC`, an IPFS link) and one creates the **master edition**, which marks the token as a true 1-of-1. Wallets and marketplaces read those two Metaplex accounts to show it as an NFT.
app_note: The fork's own create-solana-dapp React app (`web/`). The author had commented out the mint code, so **Run program** did nothing. We re-enabled that same code (same accounts, seeds and metadata) inside a mutation and wired the button to it; the full diff is [tests/devnet/patches/gree.patch](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/patches/gree.patch). Also: base path, hash routing for static hosting, this program ID.

try_steps.do: Open [the app](/dapps/gree/#/gree) and connect Phantom with **Select Wallet** in the top bar. Check the cluster selector says devnet.
try_steps.see: The gree page with a **Run program** button.
One transaction. When it confirms, the page shows `Minted NFT: <address>` linking to Explorer, and a toast with the transaction.
On Explorer: a token with supply 1 and 0 decimals, and a Metadata section with the name GLC-20240317 and symbol GRLC.
The new NFT in your wallet (the image comes from the author's IPFS link, so it can take a while to appear or may not load).
A second, different NFT: the app generates a fresh mint keypair every time.

diagram:
Run program ─▶ init_nft(name, symbol, uri)      signers: your wallet + a fresh mint keypair
  1. init Mint (decimals 0, authority = you)                     [Token program, via Anchor init]
  2. init_if_needed your associated token account
  3. mint_to(1) ─────────────────────────────▶ Token program        supply = 1
  4. create_metadata_accounts_v3 ────────────▶ Metaplex  Metadata PDA ["metadata", metaplex, mint]
  5. create_master_edition_v3 ───────────────▶ Metaplex  Edition  PDA ["metadata", metaplex, mint, "edition"]
                                                       (Metaplex takes over the mint authority: no more tokens)
accounts: A new keypair generated by the app (co-signs)
PDA **of the Metaplex program**: `["metadata", metaplex_id, mint]`
Marks the 1-of-1 and holds the mint authority afterwards

instructions.name: `init_nft` step 1: create the mint and mint one token
steps: `#[account(init, mint::decimals = 0, mint::authority = signer, ...)]` makes Anchor create and initialise the mint account before your code runs. Because the mint is a brand-new account, its keypair must sign the transaction too.
`init_if_needed` with `associated_token::mint/authority` creates your token account if you don't have one for this mint.
`mint_to(cpi_context, 1)` calls the Token program to mint exactly 1 base unit. With 0 decimals, that is one whole, indivisible token.

instructions.name: `init_nft` step 2: attach Metaplex metadata
steps: `DataV2` holds name, symbol and URI (passed in by the app), 0 royalties and no creators or collection.
`create_metadata_accounts_v3(ctx, data, false, true, None)`: `is_mutable = false` locks the metadata forever; `update_authority_is_signer = true`.
The metadata account is created and owned by the Metaplex program, not by gree: gree only passes the address and pays.

instructions.name: `init_nft` step 3: the master edition
steps: `create_master_edition_v3(ctx, None)` creates the edition account. Metaplex takes the mint and freeze authority from you as part of this call, so nobody can ever mint a second token of this mint.

innovation.title: checking another program's PDAs with `seeds::program`
innovation.text: The metadata and master-edition accounts are PDAs of the **Metaplex** program, not of gree. Anchor's `seeds::program = token_metadata_program.key()` tells Anchor to derive them with Metaplex's program ID, so gree verifies that the app passed the right addresses before handing them to Metaplex in the CPI. One instruction, three programs (Token, Associated Token, Metaplex), and every address is checked.
more: Doing mint + metadata + edition in a single instruction means the NFT can never exist half-made: if any CPI fails, the whole transaction, including the mint, is rolled back.
Re-using a mint fails at step 1: Anchor's `init` refuses an account that already exists (custom program error 0x0 in Proof).

frontend.title: The author's original (commented-out) client code

refs.note: as found in the fork: commented out, and initNft is not returned

steps: The fork shipped this code commented out, so the button had no handler. It already had the full recipe: new mint keypair, ATA, and the two Metaplex PDAs derived with `findMetadataPda` / `findMasterEditionPda`.

frontend.title: What runs on Sol.College: the same code inside a mutation

refs.note: our patch, + lines are the live code

steps: `anchor.web3.Keypair.generate()` makes the new mint; `.signers([mint])` adds its signature next to the wallet's.
`findMetadataPda` and `findMasterEditionPda` (Metaplex UMI helpers) compute the same addresses the program checks with `seeds::program`.
`.accounts({...})` passes all ten accounts, including the Token, Associated Token and Metaplex program IDs, and `.rpc()` sends through Phantom.

frontend.title: The button
steps: `onClick={() => initNft.mutateAsync()}`; when the mutation returns, the page prints the mint address with an Explorer link.

exercises.title: Inspect a minted NFT
steps: Open the mint `9Shg8nhKPC86hFC4wpn2a5SFFP7t4iJfPCEvD72cxHzB` from our recorded run on Solana Explorer (devnet).
exercises.expect: Supply 1, decimals 0, metadata name GLC-20240317 and symbol GRLC, metadata owned by `metaqbxxUerdq28cj1RbAWkYQm3ybzjb6a8bt518x1s` (the Metaplex program).
exercises.hint: The mint address is in the transaction that the app shows you, and on Explorer under Token → Mint.
exercises.approach: Open the mint on Explorer (devnet): supply 1, decimals 0, and no mint authority (it was set to `None` after minting, which is what locks the supply). The metadata account is a PDA you will derive in the next exercise.

exercises.title: Derive the metadata address yourself
steps: In Node: `PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync([Buffer.from('metadata'), META.toBuffer(), mint.toBuffer()], META)` with `META = metaqbxxUerdq28cj1RbAWkYQm3ybzjb6a8bt518x1s` and your mint.
exercises.expect: The same metadata address Explorer shows for your NFT. Add `Buffer.from('edition')` as a 4th seed to get the master edition.
exercises.hint: Metaplex's seeds are `"metadata"`, the metadata program id, and the mint — and the PDA is derived *under the metadata program*, not under this program.
exercises.approach: `findProgramAddressSync([Buffer.from('metadata'), METADATA_PROGRAM.toBuffer(), mint.toBuffer()], METADATA_PROGRAM)` with `metaqbxxUerdq28cj1RbAWkYQm3ybzjb6a8bt518x1s`. It must equal the metadata account in the mint transaction.

exercises.title: See that the supply is locked
steps: On Explorer, open your mint and read its mint authority.
exercises.expect: It is no longer your wallet: Metaplex moved it to the master edition account, so no one can mint a second copy.
exercises.hint: A mint with a leftover mint authority can still mint more, so '1 of 1' would be a promise, not a fact.
exercises.approach: On Explorer, confirm Mint authority is empty. In the program, find the CPI that sets the mint authority to `None` after minting one token. That, not the metadata, is what makes the NFT non-fungible.

exercises.title: Your own name and symbol
steps: Change `metadata.name` and `metadata.symbol` in the app's mutation (lines 65–69 of the patched file) and rebuild the app (`dapps/static_build.sh gree <clone>`), or call `initNft('MyNFT','MINE', uri)` from a script.
exercises.expect: Explorer shows your name and symbol on the new mint; the program needs no change, because name, symbol and URI are instruction arguments.
exercises.hint: The name and symbol the instruction takes are just arguments; the app can pass anything within the program's length limits.
exercises.approach: Call the instruction (or use the app, if it exposes the fields) with your own name and symbol, then read the metadata account: it should show exactly what you passed, at the same mint.

exercises.title: Break it on purpose
steps: From a script, call `init_nft` twice with the same mint keypair.
exercises.expect: The second call fails with `custom program error: 0x0` (account already in use), as in Proof.
exercises.hint: The program has length and emptiness checks on the metadata fields. Sending an empty name is the cheapest way to see a custom error.
exercises.approach: From a local test, send an empty name or a string over the max length. You should get the program's own error, not a generic transaction failure, and no mint should be created.

objectives: Follow a single instruction that mints one token and, in the same transaction, makes a CPI to Metaplex to attach name, symbol and URI.
Derive the metadata PDA the same way Metaplex does, and confirm the mint's supply is 1 and its mint authority is empty.
See why a program signs a CPI as a PDA (`invoke_signed`) when it is the mint authority.
prereqs: Phantom on devnet and about 0.1 devnet SOL (minting creates several accounts).
[Proof of Estimate](/lessons/poe-solana/) or equivalent: you have seen a PDA-signed CPI to the Token Program.

build.note: The program lives under `anchor/`. It depends on `anchor-spl` with the `metadata` feature (Metaplex).
